gloss: be done (passive); can (potential); honorific (after ichidan verbs)

definitions.gloss: passive: to be done (to); to have something done to one
definitions.explanation: Attached to ichidan verbs and {来|く}る, it makes the passive: {見|み}る → {見|み}られる (be seen), {食|た}べる → {食|た}べられる (be eaten), {来|く}る → {来|こ}られる. The doer is marked with に. Japanese also uses the passive for things that happen to one against one's wishes, even with intransitive verbs: {雨|あめ}に{降|ふ}られる (be rained on). Godan verbs take れる instead, and する becomes される.

definitions.gloss: potential: can do; to be able to
definitions.explanation: The same form expresses ability or possibility: {起|お}きられる (can get up), {来|こ}られる (can come). The object of a potential verb is often marked with が instead of を: {納豆|なっとう}が{食|た}べられる.

The same form also shows respect for the person doing the action: {先生|せんせい}が{来|こ}られた (the teacher came). It is lighter than special honorific verbs such as いらっしゃる and is common in news and business writing.

examples.japanese: ⟦{弟|おとうと}→弟：00572_otouto⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ケーキ→ケーキ：01356_keeki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べられた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: My little brother ate my cake (on me).

examples.japanese: ⟦{電車|でんしゃ}→電車：00522_densha⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{知|し}らない→知る：00458_shiru⟧⟦{人|ひと}→人：00476_hito⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{話|はな}しかけられて→話しかける：03134_hanashikakeru⟧、⟦{少|すこ}し→少し：00596_sukoshi⟧⟦{困|こま}った→困る：00861_komaru⟧。
examples.english: A stranger started talking to me on the train, and I was a bit at a loss.

examples.japanese: ⟦{朝|あさ}→朝：02277_asa⟧⟦{六時|ろくじ}→六時：10982_rokuji⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{起|お}き→起きる：00521_okiru⟧られる？
examples.english: Can you get up at six in the morning?

examples.japanese: ⟦{明日|あした}→明日：00501_ashita⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{来|こ}られます⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧。
examples.english: Will you be able to come tomorrow?

examples.japanese: {子|こ}ども⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ころ→頃：32850_koro⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{嫌|きら}い→嫌い：02871_kirai⟧だった⟦ピーマン→ピーマン：11132_piiman⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧、⟦{今|いま}→今：00945_ima⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{食|た}べ→食べる：00396_taberu⟧られるようになった。
examples.english: I hated green peppers as a child, but now I can eat them.

examples.japanese: ⟦{社長|しゃちょう}→社長：01428_shachou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{来|こ}られました。
⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦もう→もう：00602_mou⟧⟦{帰|かえ}る→帰る：00508_kaeru⟧⟦{準備|じゅんび}→準備：01431_junbi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{始|はじ}められた。
examples.english: The teacher has already started getting ready to leave.

examples.japanese: ⟦{部長|ぶちょう}→部長：01017_buchou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{来月|らいげつ}→来月：00744_raigetsu⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦ロンドン→ロンドン：30808_rondon⟧⟦{支社|ししゃ}→支社：31747_shisha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{勤|つと}め→勤める：00902_tsutomeru⟧られるそうです。
examples.english: I hear the department head will be working at the London branch from next month.

notes:
FORMS:
The result conjugates as an ichidan verb: ⟦{見|み}られない→見る：00283_miru⟧, ⟦{見|み}られた→見る：00283_miru⟧, ⟦{見|み}られて→見る：00283_miru⟧. Which of the three meanings is meant depends on the context and the particles: ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{見|み}られた→見る：00283_miru⟧ (seen by the teacher, passive) vs. ⟦{先生|せんせい}→先生：00609_sensei⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}られた→見る：00283_miru⟧ (the teacher saw it, honorific).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- A⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧B⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧〜られる: A is ~ed by B (passive)
- 〜られる⟦ようになる→ようになる：28408_youninaru⟧: to become able to
- spontaneous use with verbs of feeling: ⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{感|かん}じ→感じる：02044_kanjiru⟧られる (one can feel spring), ⟦{将来|しょうらい}→将来：01438_shourai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{案|あん}じ→案ずる：13144_anzuru⟧られる (one can't help worrying about the future)

WATCH OUT:
In casual speech the potential often drops ら: ⟦{見|み}れる→見る：00283_miru⟧, {来|こ}れる, ⟦{食|た}べれる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧ (ら{抜|ぬ}き⟦{言葉|ことば}→言葉：02880_kotoba⟧). It is widespread but still counts as nonstandard in writing; use られる in formal contexts.
